firstOccurrence.englishText: One who had escaped came and told Abram, the Hebrew. At that time, he lived by the oaks of Mamre, the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner. They were allies of Abram.

timeline.evidenceText: One who had escaped came and told Abram, the Hebrew. At that time, he lived by the oaks of Mamre, the Amorite, brother of Eshcol and brother of Aner. They were allies of Abram.
I will accept nothing from you except that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me: Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take their portion.”
They came to the valley of Eshcol, and cut down from there a branch with one cluster of grapes, and they bore it on a staff between two. They also brought some of the pomegranates and figs.
That place was called the valley of Eshcol, because of the cluster which the children of Israel cut down from there.
For when they went up to the valley of Eshcol, and saw the land, they discouraged the heart of the children of Israel, that they should not go into the land which Yahweh had given them.
They turned and went up into the hill country, and came to the valley of Eshcol, and spied it out.

definitions.short: Eshcol , the name of an Amorite, also of a valley in Palestine
definitions.full: H812. Eshkol אֶשְׁכֹּל proper name 1. masculine an Amorite, brother of Mamre, dwelling in neighbourhood of Hebron Gen 14:13 , 24 . 2 in combination אֶשְׁכֹּל נַחַל Num 13:23 ; Deut 1:24 ; ׳נ אֶשְׁכּוֺל Num 13:24 ; 32:9 ; — valley of Eshcol , = valley of a cluster , region of Hebron (compare 13:22 ); in 13:24 derived from ׳א cluster , q. v.; see however Di on the passage
